name: North Sea
genZNote: The North Sea quietly powers a chunk of Europe — oil and gas platforms out there have been part of the continent's energy story for decades.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Ocean Connection
bullets: A sea of the Atlantic Ocean between Great Britain to the west and continental North-Western Europe to the east.
Connects to the Atlantic Ocean directly in the north and to the Baltic Sea via the Danish straits in the east.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries Bordering It
bullets: United Kingdom, Norway, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, and France (a short northern coastline).

sections.heading: 🚢 Ports & Trade Routes
bullets: Rotterdam (Netherlands), one of the world's largest ports, sits right at its southern edge.
Other major ports: Antwerp (Belgium), Hamburg (Germany, via the Elbe), and Felixstowe (UK).
One of the busiest seas in the world for both cargo shipping and offshore energy infrastructure.

sections.heading: 🐠 Economic & Ecological Significance
bullets: A historically major fishing ground, particularly for cod and herring, now managed under strict EU/UK fisheries quotas after decades of overfishing pressure.
Contains significant offshore oil and gas fields that have supplied a large share of the UK's and Norway's energy for decades.
Increasingly important for offshore wind energy, with some of the world's largest offshore wind farms built in its shallow waters.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The North Sea is a busy Atlantic sea between Great Britain and North-Western Europe, historically important for fishing and oil/gas, now also a major offshore wind hub.
keyFacts: Borders UK, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Netherlands, Belgium, France.
Rotterdam sits at its southern edge — one of the world's largest ports.
Major historic fishing ground; major offshore oil/gas region.
commonConfusion: The North Sea and the Baltic Sea are separate seas connected by the narrow Danish straits, not the same body of water.

highYieldFacts: North Sea = between UK and North-Western Europe.
Rotterdam (world's largest European port) sits at its southern edge.
Historic oil/gas region, now also major for offshore wind.
commonTraps: Don't merge the North Sea's oil/gas history with the Arctic's untapped resource potential — they're geographically distinct regions.
mustRemember: North Sea = UK/NW Europe's key sea; Rotterdam; oil/gas + offshore wind.
